overview: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas, made up of two islands in the eastern Caribbean. Its capital, Basseterre, is on Saint Kitts. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1983. The country is a federation, and Nevis has its own island government.

geography.text: Both islands are volcanic, with rainforest-covered mountains in the centre; Mount Liamuiga on Saint Kitts is the highest point. The two islands are separated by a channel only about three kilometres wide, called The Narrows.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical, cooled by sea breezes, with a hurricane season.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Green vervet monkeys, brought from Africa in the 1600s, may outnumber people.

history.text: Saint Kitts was the first Caribbean island settled by the English, in 1623, and the French also settled part of it; together they drove out and killed most of the island's Kalinago people in 1626. Sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans dominated for centuries. Saint Kitts and Nevis became independent in 1983.

events.title: English settlement
events.text: The first English colony in the Caribbean is founded.

events.title: Kalinago massacre
events.text: English and French settlers kill most of the Kalinago people.

events.title: Alexander Hamilton born
events.text: A future founder of the United States is born on Nevis.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis becomes independent.

government.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a federal constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor-General, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Nevis has its own assembly and the right to leave the federation by referendum.

economy.text: Tourism and the sale of citizenship to foreign investors are the main sources of income. The sugar industry, which dominated for centuries, closed in 2005.

culture.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas. Brimstone Hill Fortress, built by the British, is a UNESCO site. Alexander Hamilton, one of the founders of the United States, was born on Nevis.

items.title: Brimstone Hill Fortress
items.text: A hilltop fortress called the 'Gibraltar of the West Indies'.

items.title: Sugar train
items.text: The old sugar cane railway now carries tourists.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Stewed saltfish with dumplings and breadfruit is the national dish.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Calypso and soca, and the Saint Kitts Music Festival every June.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Sugar Mas, the Christmas and New Year carnival, has masquerade dancers in colourful costumes.

sport.text: Cricket and athletics are the most popular sports. Kim Collins won the 100 m world championship in 2003, the country's greatest sporting moment.

items.text: Kim Collins became 100 m world champion.

didYouKnow: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas by area and population.
A sugar train once circled Saint Kitts carrying cane to the mill; tourists ride it today.
